newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares end down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares end down on profit-taking.

text.p: Jakarta share prices ended lower in active trade on Tuesday, pushed down by investors shedding positions in some blue chips led by Indofood and Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI), brokers said.
They also said profit-taking in secondaries which had made recent gains on speculation also helped pull down the index.
The Jakarta Composite Index fell 4.59 points, or 0.66 percent, to close at 695.52 points after earlier falling to 692.30 points.
In the broader market, losers led gainers by 91 to 47, with 53 counters unchanged. Total volume was 720 billion rupiah on a volume of 265 million shares.
Brokers said the market was likely to be mixed on Wednesday due to possible continued profit-taking in BNI, Indofood and Indocement.
But they said that a favourable announcement on February inflation, scheduled to be made after the regular cabinet meeting on Wednesday, could boost sentiment.

State-controlled BNI fell 50 rupiah to 1,650 rupiah on a turnover of about 10 million shares after it announced an unaudited 1996 net profit of 335 billion rupiah, compared with a consensus estimate of 324.6 billion rupiah.
"The result was in line with my target of about 333 billion rupiah," said BZW Niaga Securities analyst Mirza Adityaswara, adding however that the prevailing price of 1,650 rupiah was quite expensive.

He said profit taking in BNI could have emerged from high expectations of some investors, particularly local players, who held the stocks in expectation that it might book higher 1996 earnings. Mirza said the fair price for BNI would be at around 1,400 rupiah to 1,450 rupiah.
Blue-chips belonging to the Salim group, Indofood and Indocement, were among the target of foreign sellers, brokers said.
Noodle maker Indofood fell 50 rupiah to 5,175 rupiah on 1.6 million shares volume as many analysts were not enthusiastic about its internal acquisition plan, brokers said.
They added its sister company Indocement received a spill- over effect and ended down 50 rupiah to 3,450 rupiah on 1.1 million shares traded.

Secondary Hotel Sahid Jaya was the most active stock with 14.3 million shares traded, falling 100 rupiah to 1,800 on profit-taking after touching a high of 2,225 rupiah earlier on market speculation of a possible rights issue.
